skill.name: azure-resource-manager-sql-dotnet
skill.description: Guidance for using Azure.ResourceManager.Sql in .NET to provision and manage Azure SQL servers, databases, elastic pools, firewall rules, and related resources.
skill.summary: Use Azure.ResourceManager.Sql examples to manage Azure SQL resources with .NET.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline code, not executable Ruby backticks. The 0.0.0.0 Azure SQL firewall example is a real network exposure risk, and the public access sample adds related cloud configuration risk. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious execution flow was found.

remediation.issue: Permissive Azure SQL public access example
remediation.suggestion: Default examples to private endpoints or disabled public network access. Show public access only as an explicit development option.

remediation.issue: Firewall rule uses the 0.0.0.0 Azure services sentinel
remediation.suggestion: Explain that 0.0.0.0 allows Azure services and replace it with least-privilege client IP placeholders where possible.

remediation.issue: Credential environment variables appear in setup guidance
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to keep secrets out of prompts, logs, and source control. Prefer managed identity when available.

content.user_title: Manage Azure SQL with .NET ARM SDK
content.value_statement: Azure SQL management tasks require correct ARM SDK types, authentication, and long-running operation handling. This skill provides .NET examples for servers, databases, elastic pools, firewall rules, and connection settings.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation commands for Azure.ResourceManager.Sql and Azure.Identity.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential setup with subscription resource access.
Provides .NET samples to create SQL servers, databases, and elastic pools.
Demonstrates adding databases to elastic pools and listing SQL resources.
Includes firewall rule examples, SKU references, and ARM error handling.
Distinguishes Azure SQL management plane tasks from data plane SDK usage.
limitations: Does not validate current Azure SDK versions or service availability.
Does not execute deployments or confirm permissions in an Azure subscription.
Example networking settings require security review before production use.
Reference files named in the skill are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Prototype Azure SQL provisioning
use_cases.description: Build a small .NET workflow that creates a server, database, and basic resource settings.

use_cases.title: Standardize SQL resource operations
use_cases.description: Create repeatable ARM SDK patterns for databases, elastic pools, firewall rules, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Review SDK boundaries
use_cases.description: Decide when to use Azure.ResourceManager.Sql instead of data plane SQL libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic server
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create an Azure SQL server with Azure.ResourceManager.Sql and DefaultAzureCredential. Include required inputs and safety notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add a database
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add an Azure SQL database to an existing server using the .NET ARM SDK. Explain SKU choices and long-running operations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan elastic pools
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Azure.ResourceManager.Sql workflow for creating an elastic pool and adding databases. Include capacity considerations and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design secure production workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure SQL ARM SDK deployment plan for production. Focus on identity, private networking, firewall scope, idempotency, and error handling.

output_examples.input: I need to create an S0 Azure SQL database in an existing server.
output: Confirm subscription, resource group, server, region, database name, and SKU.
Use the server database collection and wait for the create or update operation to finish.
Review firewall access before testing client connectivity.

output_examples.input: I want several low-traffic databases to share capacity.
output: Use an elastic pool when databases have variable or shared demand.
Choose a pool tier and capacity before assigning databases.
Track per-database minimum and maximum capacity limits.

output_examples.input: I am unsure which Azure SQL SDK to use.
output_examples.output: Use Azure.ResourceManager.Sql for provisioning and configuration. Use Microsoft.Data.SqlClient for queries, transactions, and application data access.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and avoid placing secrets in source files or prompts.
Prefer private networking and narrowly scoped firewall rules for production databases.
Handle RequestFailedException and make create or update operations idempotent.
anti_patterns: Do not copy broad firewall examples into production without security review.
Do not place SQL admin passwords in prompts, logs, or source control.
Do not use the management plane SDK for querying or modifying table data.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps generate and review .NET ARM SDK patterns for managing Azure SQL resources.

faq.question: Does it run Azure deployments?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users must run and validate changes in their own environment.

faq.question: Which authentication approach does it show?
faq.answer: It shows DefaultAzureCredential and environment-based Azure identity setup for development or automation contexts.

faq.question: Can it help with SQL queries?
faq.answer: Only at a high level. Use Microsoft.Data.SqlClient or an ORM for database queries and data access.

faq.question: Are the firewall examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Review them carefully and prefer private endpoints or narrowly scoped client access.

faq.question: Does it include all referenced files?
faq.answer: No. The package contains the main skill file, but referenced detailed files are not included.
